text: The case status stays rwb-case's. rwb-treatment reports a stage outcome to the parent CaseWorkflow and the parent moves the status and raises the task; no case table is read or written by this service (DP-01).
why: AC2 of RWB-E3-016 ends with the case moving to RENTAL_RUNNING and R-DIL-34 ends with the asset handed to disposal, while Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the case and its CMMN state to rwb-case and DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables.

impact: If the parent does not own the transition, a stage would have to signal rwb-case over REST and a C dependency would appear on the plan; no business rule changes either way.

text: The rental record is a treatment row of type RENTAL of LOV-TREATMENT on the same case, with the agreed rent in offer_amount (DF-TRT-007), the first rental due date in first_due_date (DF-TRT-029) and the instalments paid in installments_paid (DF-TRT-032); no rental table and no tenancy table is created.
why: R-DIL-32 says create the rental record, the TSD stops at DF-TRT-033 with no rental table and no rental field, the service owns one table (treatment), and a table of its own would record the same tenancy twice, once as a row and once as a record, which DP-01 and Principle 5 forbid.
read: TSD S2 T3.1 (treatment, DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033; DF-TRT-007 offer_amount, DF-TRT-029 first_due_date, DF-TRT-032 installments_paid) and T3.2 (LOV-TREATMENT carries RENTAL and BUY_BACK, LOV-TRT-OUTCOME carries KEPT, BROKEN, COMPLETED, CANCELED and DECLINED); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 row R-DIL-32; Ownership Map row treatment (owner S2); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-03

text: The ACE customer and NPA-asset facts a buy-back rental needs arrive on the case signal as facts of rwb-source-data's read; rwb-treatment reads no v_ace_* view and calls no source-data service, because the connection matrix gives it no such link.
why: The legacy data table reads v_ace_customer (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074) and v_ace_npa_asset (DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219) directly, while DP-05 sends ACE data through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own views, slide 8 grants the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone, and slide 13 gives the S2 row no cell for P1.

text: The AMIS rental record, the ATS auto-debit mandate and the disposal hand-off are requested through rwb-asset and rwb-integration and return as facts on the workflow; this service calls no external system and the Work Package's empty external list stands.
why: R-DIL-32 requires the rental record and the auto-debit to be created and names ATS and AMIS as the systems of the step, the legacy service calls them in process, TSD T5.1 names INT-03 core bank (ALS), INT-26 NLEADS and INT-34 ACE common but no AMIS and no ATS interface, and the Work Package declares no external and no integration dependency.

text: The receipt loop is rwb-payment's: a matched rental instalment arrives as a fact on the case signal and increments installments_paid, a missed instalment arrives as rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 (EV-12) on this service's inbox, and the rental start reaches rwb-payment through the case events of rwb-case because no source names a rental event.
why: REQ-S2-010 and FEAT-TRT-16 require the receipts and the arrears follow-up to run without a person, the legacy story matches proceeds in its own code, the catalogue gives rwb-treatment one event (EV-10) and names none for the rental, and the connection matrix gives the S2 row a Kafka listen to P8 and the P3 row a Kafka publish to P8.

text: The embedded Drools runtime, the DEEDINLIEU rule package and the workflow kit with its timers and outbox are the service template's wave-0 capability; this story names the evaluated package and its version and adds no build dependency of its own beyond the three the Work Package lists.
why: Every criterion ends with the result written with its rule version, Architecture v5 slide 18 runs the DIL rule set in rwb-treatment, and the Work Package's patterns are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 with no Drools or workflow-kit contract among its H dependencies.

text: The rental facts not published on the treatment are held on the treatment row as rentalRef, autoDebitRef and autoDebitStatus, the rent is carried as offer_amount (DF-TRT-007), the first rental due date as first_due_date (DF-TRT-029) and the instalments paid as installments_paid (DF-TRT-032), the mandate state is deferred to its owner, and no rental table and no rental event is created.
why: The TSD stops at DF-TRT-033 with no such element, the API Specification publishes no treatment element for them, no list of values carries a mandate state, and the catalogue gives the service one event; a table or an event of its own would let the same tenancy be recorded twice, which DP-01, DP-03 and Principle 5 forbid.
